title: Generation of a module derived category by shifts of the ring
statement: For a ring $A$, let $D(A)$ be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of $A$-modules. Every object $K$ of $D(A)$ belongs to the smallest full subcategory of $D(A)$ that contains all shifts $A[k]$, $k\in\mathbf Z$, and is closed under set-indexed direct sums, under the third vertex of a distinguished triangle whose other two vertices lie in it, and under retracts.

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark 15.60.11 (more-algebra-remark-P-resolution), Tag 09PB, as invoked in perfect.tex Lemma 36.22.1 (Tag 08EU)

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-derived-module-cellular-filtration] to obtain L,F, compatible monomorphisms, exhaustion, an isomorphism K≅Q(L), a zero initial object, and coproduct/triangle data for each cell.
Apply coproduct closure to the empty family to prove P(Q(F_0)). Induct on n: generator closure and coproduct closure give P(G_n), and the cellular triangle gives P(Q(F_{n+1})).
Apply [lem-pc-derived-module-filtration-telescope] to the exhaustive filtration. Coproduct closure gives P(S); the triangle S→S→Q(L) gives P(Q(L)).
The isomorphism K≅Q(L) gives Retract K (Q(L)); apply the supplied retract closure hypothesis.

statement_change.old_statement: For a ring $A$, every object $K$ of $D(A)$ [def-pc-derived-category] belongs to the smallest full subcategory of $D(A)$ that contains all shifts $A[k]$, $k\in\mathbf Z$, and is closed under set-indexed direct sums, under the third vertex of a distinguished triangle whose other two vertices lie in it, and under retracts.
statement_change.what: The cited dependency def-pc-derived-category defines D(O_X) for a scheme X, so it does not introduce D(A) for a ring A; the original statement therefore had an undefined and mismatched derived category. The corrected statement follows the source and cites the general derived category of an abelian category.
